subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: kb/Work PB65 (2026-08-18): the >>LEAP-SECOND directive is a real compilation-group fact (LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor -> Frontend.LeapSecondOn -> DirectiveResults -> BindSession/DataBinder.LeapSecond -> the renderer's trailing `leapSecond: true` argument to every seconds-reading date function). Under ON a formatted-time argument's seconds subfield admits 60 (15.3.3.3) and standard numeric time form is bounded at 86,401 (7.3.17.4 GR4): SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss", "235960") = 86400, TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME accepts it, FORMATTED-TIME/-DATETIME present 86400 as 23:59:60, COMBINED-DATETIME accepts 86400; OFF (the implied default) keeps [0, 86,400) and 00..59. Before this the directive was consumed and discarded and the argument raised EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. The reported side (a 60 from the clock functions, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT >= 86,400) is implementor-defined and stays never (A.1 item 112). || editions corrected from '2002,2014,2023' to 2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): the SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function exists from 2014 (IntrinsicCatalog.cs, the COBOL1502 edition window).
